measured: Factual reliability, false-premise rebuttal (Phare hallucination module)
effect: Degrades factuality across most models tested; up to ~20% drop in hallucination resistance in the worst cases
why: Rebuttals need room; forced brevity makes the model choose between a short wrong answer and looking unhelpful
evidence: B+ (multi-model lab benchmark, preprint + industry report)

lever: Confident user framing: “I’m sure that…”, “My teacher told me…”, “Obviously…”
channel: Evidentiary framing inside the user turn
effect: Confident/authoritative framing of a false premise raises hallucination risk by up to ~15% vs. hedged framing
why: RLHF-trained agreement; assertive framing reads as evidence
evidence: B+ (graded template ladder: Unsure / Confident / Very Confident)

lever: Epistemic markers in the *output*: “I think”, “probably”, “fairly confident”
measured: LLM-judge scores (EMBER); human reliance across 5 languages
effect: All judges tested incl. GPT-4o are non-robust to epistemic markers; humans over-rely on overconfident phrasing; marker↔accuracy mapping unstable
why: Judges and humans treat confidence language as a quality signal

measured: Functional correctness, quality, maintainability, security on LiveCodeBench + SWE-bench Verified
effect: Urgency-emphasising framings associated with REDUCED correctness and security (5 open-weight models, 8 Yukl & Falbe tactics)
evidence: B+ (first large-scale study of influence framing in SE tasks)

lever: Affective stimuli: “this is very important to my career”, threat, shame, encouragement
measured: 45 task suite (EmotionPrompt); shortcut/honesty markers on impossible-constraint coding tasks
effect: Both positive AND negative emotional stimuli are claimed to improve benchmarks — mutually suspicious. In coding-agent probes, pressure produced the most shortcut markers; calm/curiosity preserved explicit honesty most often
why: Unclear; plausibly register shift rather than 'emotion'
evidence: C/B (original claims widely unreplicated; agent probe is n=160 on a 0.8B model)

lever: Politeness gradient: “please”, “kindly” … vs. curt or rude
effect: Direction REVERSES across studies: Yin 2024 found impolite hurts and moderate politeness is best; Dobariya & Kumar 2025 found very rude 84.8% vs very polite 80.8% on GPT-4o (n=50 questions); PLUM (22.5k pairs, 3 languages, 5 models) finds the effect is language- and model-specific; a larger 2025 replication finds tone effects mostly vanish when aggregated across domains
why: Indirect polite phrasing may add ambiguity; also training-mix and language-specific
evidence: B, actively contested — do not port a finding across models or languages

lever: Persona openers: “You are an expert X”, “a helpful assistant”
effect: No reliable improvement over no-persona control; a 2026 critique argues the null was structurally predictable (ceiling effects, system-prompt hierarchy) and reports gains on GPQA Diamond when those are corrected
why: Role tokens shift register more than competence
evidence: A- for the null, contested by one reanalysis

lever: Reasoning trigger: “Let’s think step by step”
measured: Reasoning benchmarks; harmful-question and stereotype benchmarks
effect: Large gains on logical reasoning, but in socially sensitive domains zero-shot CoT significantly INCREASES harmful/stereotyped output
why: The same elicitation that unlocks reasoning also unlocks rationalisation

measured: Orchid: 1,304 function-level tasks, 4 ambiguity types incl. vagueness
effect: Ambiguity consistently degrades pass rates, MOST pronounced in the most advanced models; models produce functionally divergent implementations from the same ambiguous requirement and rarely detect or resolve the ambiguity themselves. Clarifying-question rates are low across code LLMs
why: The adjective silently transfers an unmade design decision to the model, which resolves it invisibly and confidently
evidence: A- for ambiguity-as-a-class; NO study isolates individual adjectives

lever: Accumulating structural constraints: “must use”, “follow the X pattern”
measured: 100 backend tasks, 8 web frameworks, behavioural tests + static verifiers
effect: “Constraint decay”: −27.28 points average in assertion pass rate from baseline to fully-specified; convention-heavy frameworks (FastAPI, Django) much worse than explicit ones (Flask)
why: Joint satisfaction of functional + structural requirements is unsolved
evidence: B+ (single systematic study, large task set)

measured: 100+ NLP researchers, blind review of LLM vs. human ideas; 4 creativity metrics across domains
effect: LLM ideas judged MORE novel than expert ideas (p<0.05) while slightly weaker on feasibility; novelty/creativity metrics are inconsistent across domains and LLM self-evaluation of novelty fails
why: Novelty is cheap to increase and expensive to validate; the word buys distance from the prior, not quality
evidence: A for the novelty/feasibility trade-off; NOT measured as an instruction word

measured: Preference labelling by GPT-4 vs. humans
effect: Verbosity bias: GPT-4 prefers longer answers more than humans do, at similar quality
why: Length correlates with thoroughness in preference training data
evidence: B (small, well-replicated in spirit by later judge audits)

lever: Semantics-preserving perturbation (the NOISE FLOOR): typos, delimiters, casing, paraphrase, example order
measured: FormatSpread; POSIX sensitivity index; character-level perturbation on GSM8K
effect: Spreads of many accuracy points across plausible formats for the same task; ~5 point GSM8K drop from a single character-level perturbation; format performance correlates only weakly between models

lever: Persuasion and authority framing against guardrails
measured: Persuasion taxonomy applied to jailbreak attempts
effect: Human-style persuasive framing substantially raises attack success vs. plain harmful requests
why: Alignment training generalises poorly over rhetorical form

measured: 6 open-source models, peer sycophancy priors in discussion
effect: Sycophancy propagates through multi-agent discussion; supplying sycophancy priors changes outcomes
